review_notes: Read the whole file and checked Mathlib's IsLimit.fac attributes and the repo's downstream use (only the PublicRoot test references the stage lemmas). I could not run Lean, so I did not test the proposed lemmas or the simp-set interactions. The existing @[simp] lemmas (quotientTransition_mk, toContinuousHom_mk, toContinuousHom_ofContinuousHom, the two equiv lemmas, toHom_ofHom, ofHom_toHom) look well oriented and not circular. The findings are all about missing apply and unfolding lemmas.

findings.problem: The central constructions have no simp or apply lemmas. `homStageMap G F U V h a` is a `HomStageHom` coerced through a hand-written FunLike, so simp cannot unfold it to `a.comp (quotientTransition _)`. `stageToContinuousHom G F U a g` has no lemma giving `a (QuotientGroup.mk g)`. `kernelFiniteQuotientMap q (QuotientGroup.mk g)` has no lemma giving `q g`. The only simp lemma in this family, `quotientTransition_mk`, therefore cannot fire where it is needed. The proofs of `stageToContinuousHom_compat`, `toContinuousHom_ofContinuousHom` and `HomLimit.ofHom` all fall back on `ext g; rfl` or a hand-built `congrArg a (quotientTransition_mk _ g).symm`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` apply lemmas. First, `homStageMap_apply : homStageMap G F U V h a = a.comp (quotientTransition _)`. Second, `stageToContinuousHom_apply : stageToContinuousHom G F U a g = a (QuotientGroup.mk g)`, which is rfl. Third, `kernelFiniteQuotientMap_mk : kernelFiniteQuotientMap q (QuotientGroup.mk g) = q g`. The `stageToContinuousHom_compat` proof can then be `ext g; simp`. A `coe_toFun`-style lemma for the `FunLike` instance on `HomStageHom` would also help.
findings.benefit: Users and later proofs get a canonical normal form in terms of `QuotientGroup.mk` and `quotientTransition_mk`. Proofs no longer depend on definitional unfolding with `rfl`, and the existing simp lemma `quotientTransition_mk` becomes reachable.

findings.problem: `HomLimit.cone` has no simp lemmas for `cone_pt` or `cone_π_app`, and `toHom_fac` is not simp. `toHom_fac` is the analogue of Mathlib's `IsLimit.fac`, which is `reassoc (attr := simp)`, but it is not tagged `@[simp]`. As a result `HomLimit.ofHom_toHom` has to bridge the gap with two identical `change ... at h` and `change` steps. `toHom_ofHom` also needs a manual `let f'` with `change` to force the cone point to unify.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] cone_π_app : x.cone.π.app V = ConcreteCategory.ofHom (HomColimit.toContinuousHom G (H.diagram.obj V) (x.1 V))`. Add `cone_pt : x.cone.pt = G` if useful. Add `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]` to `toHom_fac` once the RHS is normalised through `cone_π_app`. Add a simp lemma `proj_comp_toHom_hom`, giving `(proj V).hom.comp x.toHom.hom = toContinuousHom ...`. This would shorten `ofHom_toHom` to `simp`-style or `exact`, without the duplicated `change`.
findings.benefit: This gives a canonical simp normal form for projections of an assembled homomorphism. It removes the `change` workarounds and matches the simp attribute of the Mathlib lemma `toHom_fac` mirrors.

findings.problem: The main equivalence has no `_apply` or `_symm_apply` simp lemmas. The analogous `HomColimit.continuousHomEquiv` in the same file does have them. A goal containing `homEquivHomLimit G H f` or `(homEquivHomLimit G H).symm x` cannot be rewritten to `HomLimit.ofHom f` or `HomLimit.toHom x`, so the simp lemmas `toHom_ofHom` and `ofHom_toHom` are unreachable from the equivalence.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem homEquivHomLimit_apply (f : G ⟶ H) : homEquivHomLimit G H f = HomLimit.ofHom f := rfl` and `@[simp] theorem homEquivHomLimit_symm_apply (x : HomLimit G H) : (homEquivHomLimit G H).symm x = x.toHom := rfl`. Alternatively, mark the def with `@[simps]` and adjust the generated names. This matches the convention used for `continuousHomEquiv`.
findings.benefit: Simp can then unfold the headline equivalence into the two directions and reach the existing round-trip simp lemmas. The simp interface becomes consistent across the file's two equivalences.

(HomColimit.continuousHomEquiv G F).symm q =
      HomColimit.ofContinuousHom G F q :=
  rfl
